1.title: Cloud Service Types
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Cloud Service Types. It covers the exam area Describe cloud concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Describe infrastructure as a service. Describe platform as a service. Describe software as a service. Identify appropriate use cases for each cloud service type (I A A S, pass, and sass). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe cloud concepts (twenty-five to thirty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The three service types
1.text: The three service types. Cloud services are grouped by how much the provider manages for you. I A A S (infrastructure as a service). You get: Virtual machines, storage and networks. You manage: O S, middleware, runtime, apps, data. Provider manages: Datacenter, hardware, virtualization. Azure example: Azure Virtual Machines. pass (platform as a service). You get: A managed platform to build and run apps. You manage: Your application code and data. Provider manages: O S, runtime, servers, patches, scaling. Azure example: Azure App Service, Azure sequel Database.

1.title: The three service types, continued
1.text: The three service types. sass (software as a service). You get: A finished application. You manage: Your data, users and settings. Provider manages: Everything else. Azure example: Microsoft three sixty-five, Dynamics three sixty-five.

1.title: The three service types, continued
1.text: The three service types. The figure shows this: I A A S, pass and sass: what the customer and the provider manage.

1.title: The three service types, continued
1.text: The three service types. Memory aid: the further right (I A A S to pass to sass), the less you manage and the less control you have.

1.title: IaaS: infrastructure as a service
1.text: I A A S: infrastructure as a service. I A A S is the closest to a traditional datacenter. You rent virtual machines, storage and virtual networks. You choose the operating system and install software. You are responsible for patching the O S, configuring security software and managing the apps. High control, high responsibility. Use cases. Lift and shift migration: move an existing server to the cloud with few changes. Test and development environments you can create and delete quickly. Hosting apps that need a specific operating system or software setup. Backup, storage and disaster recovery capacity. Websites and apps with unpredictable load where you want full control. Exam tip: "Lift and shift" and "I patch the operating system myself" always point to I A A S.

1.title: PaaS: platform as a service
1.text: pass: platform as a service. pass gives you a ready environment for building, testing, deploying and managing applications without managing the servers and operating system. The provider patches the O S, runs the servers and often scales the platform automatically. You focus on code and data. Less control over the underlying system. Use cases. Developing and hosting web apps and A P Is without running servers. Databases as a service (managed database engines). Development frameworks and business analytics tools. Teams that want to move fast and avoid infrastructure chores.

1.title: SaaS: software as a service
1.text: sass: software as a service. sass delivers complete applications over the internet, usually through a subscription. You use the software; the provider runs it. Nothing to install or patch (usually just a browser or app). You manage your data, user accounts and settings. Least control over the software, least work. Use cases. Email and collaboration, office productivity, customer relationship tools. Business apps that are the same for many organizations. When you want to use software, not run it. Exam tip: In every service type, data, accounts and devices stay with the customer.

1.title: Choose the right type
1.text: Choose the right type. "full control of the operating system", "lift and shift", "install my own software on a server". I A A S. "focus on code only", "no O S patching", "build and deploy web apps quickly", "managed database". pass. "use a ready-made app", "email", "subscription software", "no installation". sass. Exam tip: The managed database is pass. A virtual machine you patch yourself is I A A S. Microsoft three sixty-five is sass. Serverless services such as Azure Functions are usually considered a Paa S-style model where you manage only the code.

1.title: Responsibility by type (links to Module 1)
1.text: Responsibility by type (links to Module one). Data, devices, accounts. I A A S: You. pass: You. sass: You. Applications. I A A S: You. pass: You (your own code). sass: Provider. Operating system. I A A S: You. pass: Provider. sass: Provider. Physical hosts, network, datacenter. I A A S: Provider. pass: Provider. sass: Provider.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants to move an existing server to Azure with almost no changes and keep full control of the operating system. Which service type fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: I A A S. I A A S gives virtual machines with full control of the operating system, which suits lift and shift.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A development team wants to deploy a web app without patching or managing servers. Which service type fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: pass. pass manages the O S and runtime, so the team focuses on code.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An organization wants to give staff a ready-made email and office suite with nothing to install on servers. Which service type is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: sass. sass delivers complete applications as a service.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Who is responsible for patching the guest operating system of an Azure virtual machine? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The customer. In I A A S the customer manages the operating system, including patches. (Microsoft manages the physical host.).

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which statement about sass is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The customer manages only their own data, users and settings. In sass the provider runs the application; the customer manages data, users and settings.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company uses a managed database service where the provider handles the server, O S and patching. Which type is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: pass. A managed database is pass.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What do the letters I A A S stand for? Answer: Infrastructure as a service. Question two. Which type gives the most control and the most responsibility? Answer: I A A S. Question three. Which type delivers a finished application? Answer: sass.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name an Azure pass example. Answer: Azure App Service (or Azure sequel Database). Question five. What is "lift and shift"? Answer: Moving an existing workload to the cloud with few or no changes, usually to I A A S. Question six. Who always owns the customer's data? Answer: The customer, in every service type.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. I A A S: V Ms, storage, networks; you manage O S and up; lift and shift, test and dev. pass: managed platform; you manage code and data; web apps, managed databases. sass: finished application; you manage data, users, settings; Microsoft three sixty-five. Control: most in I A A S, least in sass. Always the customer's: data, devices, accounts and identities. In the next module, we continue the course.
